accepted.question_text: For the tree of shifted standard Young tableaux ordered by containment, determine whether the identity is the only automorphism of the underlying unlabeled tree and whether each node is uniquely determined by the sequence of rank sizes in the subtree rooted at that node.

evidence.quote: 2. [Dale R. Worley] Consider the tree SSY T of shifted standard Young tableaux, with the tree structure generated by containment. Computation suggests that the only automorphism of SSY T (as an unlabeled tree) is the identity. Computation further suggests that each node of SSY T is uniquely determined by the census (cardinalities) of the ranks of the subtree rooted at the node.

accepted.question_text: For the tree of standard Young tableaux ordered by containment, determine whether every automorphism of the underlying unlabeled tree is a composition of transpose automorphisms rooted at symmetric shapes, and whether each node is determined up to transpose by the sequence of rank sizes in the subtree rooted at that node.
accepted.context_brief: automorphisms of the standard tableau tree

evidence.quote: 3. [Dale R. Worley] Consider the tree SY T of (unshifted) standard Young tableaux, with the tree structure generated by containment. For any node with a symmetric shape, there is an automorphism of SY T (as an unlabeled tree) that transposes all nodes in the subtree rooted at the node and leaves all other nodes fixed. Computation suggests that all automorphisms of SY T are compositions of these transpose automorphisms (with the identity being the composition of zero transpose automorphisms). Computation further suggests that each node of SY T is determined up to transpose by the census (cardinalities) of the ranks of the subtree rooted at the node.

accepted.question_text: For the lattice of Young diagrams with at most r rows, the general differential-poset theory yields an RSK-type correspondence from r-colored permutations into pairs of tableaux with suitable weighting. Can this theory be extended to include a notion of jeu de taquin for these diagrams and a Greene invariant for r-colored permutations that groups together exactly the permutations producing the same insertion tableau?
accepted.context_brief: jeu de taquin and Greene invariants for r-row Young diagrams

evidence.quote: 4. [Fom1994, Exam. 2.2.4] notes that lattice of Young diagrams with ≤ r rows is differential with degree r. Thus the general theory produces an RSK algorithm from r-colored permutations into pairs of such tableaux with suitable weighting. This should be expandable into similar theories as are developed for Young diagrams and shifted Young diagrams. In particular, (1) Can jeu de taquin be defined for these diagrams? (2) Can a Greene invariant be defined for r-colored permutations that groups permutations that produce the same P tableau?

accepted.question_text: For shifted Young diagrams, which are partitions into distinct parts, determine the limit-shape behavior obtained by randomly choosing a diagram of size n and scaling it by sqrt(n), and analyze the six natural measures coming from weights 1, g_lambda, g_lambda^2, c_lambda, g_lambda c_lambda, and g_lambda^2 c_lambda, where g_lambda counts shifted standard Young tableaux of shape lambda and c_lambda = 2^{|lambda| - ell(lambda)} is the shifted-RSK weighting.
accepted.context_brief: limit shapes for shifted Young diagrams

evidence.quote: 5. [Dale R. Worley] Consider the process of randomly choosing a Young diagram of size n. If we let n → ∞ and scale the diagram down by √ n in both dimensions, the average of the diagrams converges to a limit shape; points within the shape have probability 1 of being in the random diagram and points outside the shape have probability 0. Surprisingly, the same limit shape results under three distributions on the set of diagrams: uniform (weight 1), uniform on Young tableaux (weight fλ, the number of tableaux of shape λ), and the Plancherel measure (weight fλ^2). Perform the parallel analysis on shifted Young diagrams, the set of partitions into distinct parts. Since the RSK algorithm for shifted diagrams has a weighting (cλ = 2|λ|−ℓ(λ)), there are now six plausible distributions: 1, gλ, gλ^2, cλ, gλcλ, and gλ^2cλ, where gλ is the number of shifted Young tableaux (without coloring) of shape λ.

accepted.question_text: Develop a limit-shape theory for Young diagrams with at most r rows by first determining the asymptotic behavior of the r-row Young diagrams generated by r-colored permutations and then identifying a scaling regime for which a nontrivial limit shape exists.
accepted.context_brief: limit shapes for bounded-row Young diagrams

evidence.quote: 6. [Dale R. Worley] Develop a similar theory of limit shapes for Young diagrams with ≤ r rows. The initial challenge is studying the general asymptotic behavior of the r−row Young diagrams generated by r-colored permutations so that a proper scaling can be defined so that the required limit is defined.

accepted.question_text: Develop a limit-shape theory for Young-Fibonacci diagrams by defining an appropriate scaling between diagram sizes, for example through a nearly isometric doubling embedding D: YF_r(k) -> YF_r(2k), and then determine whether randomly chosen r-colored permutations admit a limit shape in the resulting limit space and, if so, identify that limit shape.

evidence.quote: 7. [Dale R. Worley] Develop a similar theory of limit shapes for Young–Fibonacci diagrams. The initial challenge is defining a concept of scaling between smaller and larger diagrams. E.g., if the scaling is a doubling, we need to define an embedding D of YFr into YFr that maps words (diagrams) of size k into words of size 2k, YF(k)r → YF(2k)r. The embedding should be “nearly isometric” in that it maps words that are “near” each other in YFr (in the distance metric of the Hasse diagram) into words that are near each other YFr, and vice-versa. And every word in YFr must be near an element of the image of D. Given such a doubling map, it defines a limit space within which the question can be asked whether randomly-chosen r-colored permutations have a limit shape. If there is a limit shape, determine it. Since YFr as dual graded graphs has a unique weighting 1, there are no colorings of the tableaux, so there are only three distributions of diagrams to be considered.

accepted.question_text: Let nu_w = S_w(1, ..., 1), the sum of the coefficients of the Schubert polynomial S_w. evidence.quote: 10. [Stan2017, sec. 4 and Conj. 4.1] via [Linus Setiabrata] Define νw = Sw(1, . . . , 1) which is the sum of the coefficients of the Schubert polynomial Sw of the permutation w. It is well-known that νw = 1 iff w is 132-avoiding (or “dominant”). Conjecture 4.1.: We have νw = 2 if and only if w = a1 · · · an has exactly one subsequence aiajak in the pattern 132, i.e., ai < ak < aj. Proved by [Weig2018, Cor. 1.3].

evidence.quote: 12. [Stan2017, sec. 1][MerSmir2015, Ques. 5.6] via [Linus Setiabrata] Define νw = Sw(1, . . . , 1) which is the sum of the coefficients of the Schubert polynomial Sw. accepted.question_text: In the Young-Fibonacci lattices YF_r, do there exist sequences of elements (p_i)_{i >= 0} such that for every n the intervals [p_n, p_{n+k}] are all isomorphic as k varies, and if such sequences exist can they be used to prove an analog of the interval-stability result described in the paper and thereby suggest a semi-distributive property of YF_r?

evidence.quote: 43. A central point of [LiangSag2024, Th. 3.1] is that for any partition λ, the set of partitions (λ + i)i≥0 has the property that for every n, the set of intervals {[λ + n, λ + (n + k)] | k ≥ 0} are all isomorphic. Similar series of elements can be found in other distributive Fomin lattices, the lattice of strict partitions, the lattice of k-row partitions, and the cylindric partitions. Can this observation be extended to the Young–Fibonacci lattices? That is, are there sequences of elements in YFr, (pi)i≥0 for which for every n, the set of intervals {[pn, pn+k] | k ≥ 0} are all isomorphic? If there are, can they be used to prove an analog of Th. 3.1? If so, does this provide a clue to a “semi-distributive” property of YFr?

accepted.question_text: Suppose an r-vector is an arithmetic progression with difference Delta. Beyond the Cartesian exponentials of the 2-element and 3-element chains, do there exist any finite distributive differential posets with such r-vectors when Delta < 0, and can all Delta < 0 cases be classified completely?

evidence.quote: 44. [Stan1990, sec. 2] For any vector r there is at most one r-differential distributive lattice L(r). If we consider the class of r-vectors that are arithmetic progressions with a given difference ∆, then the class L(r) of differential lattices that are differential posets with such r-vectors is closed under cartesian products. Applying known results shows that ∆ ≤ 0. If ∆ = 0, they are ordinary differential posets. But if ∆ < 0, they must be finite. Do there exist any finite distributive differential posts with r-vectors that are arithmetic progressions other than the cartesian exponentials of the 2- and 3-element chains? Can the cases with ∆ < 0 be fully classified?

evidence.quote: 45. [Fom1994, sec. 2.3]. Given a graded vector space V = ⊕∞ i=0 Vi and a graded linear operator D on it where D(V0) = {0}, is it always possible to define a bilinear product on V that turns it into a graded algebra with identity for which D is a derivation — D(ab) = D(a)b + aD(b)? It seems that one can always define such a product, but there is much freedom and no clear guarantee the product has any nice properties. So let us add that the product must be associative.
